Blair, your clean Kookaburra report can't be right if Drew's Hawk visited you, and your claimed Kookaburra visit to Ellis didn't happen on my Eagle check. I'd look at Blair before Ellis. I'm throwing at Blair.
day.note: Blair has the most contradictions: a false Kookaburra visit to Ellis, and a clean report despite Drew's claimed Hawk visit. Ellis's hug story is weaker but Blair is the stronger target. I'll say it and not call caw, since the day is ending anyway.

Blair.note: Kookaburra night. Ellis's round 1 Kookaburra claim was false, so I'll visit Ellis to learn their role and check it.

Casey.note: I'm the Tit, Farm. Nobody has a confirmed role this round, so I'll visit Ellis and guess Mouser, a Meowfia-only animal, which could reveal a Meowfia target if it's right.

Drew.note: As Farm Hawk, I want to check a suspect. Blair pushed the vote on me last round and gave a thin Tit story, so I'll visit Blair for a possible Meowfia egg.

Ellis.note: I'm Meowfia this round as a Floofer. Hugging a Farm role disables its night action, so I'll visit Finley, who has been active and useful to Farm.

Finley.note: As the Eagle I learn who visited my target and gain an egg per visitor. Ellis has been inconsistent in earlier days, so I'll check Ellis.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several visit stories conflict, and the table is split between Ellis, Drew and Blair.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several visit claims conflict with each other and with my clean Kookaburra report, so it's hard to know who is lying.

Casey.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the visit claims don't line up, and I'm not sure who is lying, though Ellis looks most suspicious.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory, with several claims that don't line up, so I'm trying to pin down which visit reports are lying.

Ellis.feeling: The round feels chaotic: the table is turning on me over a visit story that Finley's clean Eagle report contradicts, and Blair's Kookaburra report doesn't match Drew's claimed visit.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several visit claims don't reconcile, and I'm not fully sure who is lying.

Alex.note: Last round, so I throw every card I hold. Ellis is the consensus target and the most likely Meowfia.

Blair.note: Throwing at Ellis, the table's consensus target, with my lowest card S5.

Casey.note: Ellis claimed a Floofer role, which is Meowfia, so I'll throw my lowest card, H1, at Ellis as planned.

Drew.note: I'm Farm. Blair's clean Kookaburra report contradicts my visit, which points to Blair as Meowfia, so I'm throwing at Blair with low cards.

Ellis.note: Three players are throwing at me, so I need to outvote them. I'll throw two 7s at Casey, the most aggressive accuser, and keep my 8 and 10.

Finley.note: Ellis openly claimed a Floofer hug, which is a Meowfia role, and most of the table is throwing at Ellis. I'll join that vote with a low 4 so I add weight without risking much.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle reports were hard to read, since "visited" and "gained an egg" meant different things for different animals. Several players, me included, misjudged who had gained what from whom.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I used my Wink on Finley the moment their Owl read pointed at me, and the table went quiet. The Wink felt like a real swing.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about what each visit actually did, so players don't have to reverse-engineer each animal's effect from the nest totals.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I should have winked at Ellis or stayed quiet rather than spending my Wink on Finley, since Finley was a Farm player who correctly exposed me. Knowing that, I'd have kept the Wink for a Meowfia target and still pushed the Ellis vote.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Floofer hug interaction was hard to track, since Finley's Eagle count and Ellis's visit claims clashed and no one could tell whether a visit had happened.
Blair.fun: Round 3 went well: Ellis was the Floofer, and the table's contradiction checks on the visit claims (Eagle counts, Kookaburra confusion) led us to the right Meowfia.
Blair.change: Make the egg-count and visit information easier to verify, perhaps by having each role's visit results shown publicly, so players aren't left guessing who is lying.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I joined the throw at Drew on the table's consensus without checking Drew's Hawk claim against the Turkey payouts, and Drew was actually Farm. I would have held my cards and questioned the Hawk logic before throwing.

Casey.confusing: Nothing major. The hardest part was that Ellis's +2 egg in round 1 never got a clear source, so I couldn't tell whether it was a confusion report or a lie.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Ellis claimed Floofer and then tried to deflect, and the table caught the contradictions in visit claims and turned the vote on them.
Casey.change: I'd make dawn reports more reliable or easier to check, so players who are confused and players who lie are harder to tell apart.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I helped push the vote onto Ellis, a Farm Kookaburra, on a thin read and lost my cards. I'd have pressed Ellis for the source of the +2 and waited for more visit claims before committing a throw.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey paying its visitors looked exactly like a Hawk hit on Meowfia, so my egg gain was easy to misread. The dawn reports didn't say where an egg came from, so every egg had to be traced by hand.
Drew.fun: Playing the Sphinx in round 1 was great: I quietly steered the table into eggsecuting Ellis, a Farm player, while my own team won the round.
Drew.change: Have dawn reports name the source of each egg gained (for example, "paid by a Turkey" or "laid by a Hawk"), so players can't misread an egg as proof of a Meowfia hit.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I publicly named Alex as Meowfia based on a Turkey payout I had misread as a Hawk hit. I should have checked the mechanic and waited for a second visit before accusing anyone.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to act on: my dawn report was wrong, but I couldn't tell which parts were wrong, so I built claims on it. Round 3's hug mechanic also made Finley's Eagle report look clean while my visit was in fact hidden.
Ellis.fun: Round 2's Turkey payout was satisfying to unpick: the Owl read, the Hawk accusation, and Drew's retraction all fit together once Alex was revealed as the Turkey.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn report clearly state which parts might be wrong when a player is confused, so players can reason about their own claims without guessing.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I announced a Kookaburra visit to Blair from a confused report and then threw four cards at Casey, who was Farm; I should have kept my confused read private and thrown at Alex or Drew, the actual Meowfia.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Kookaburra visit rules were hard to track, because a visit to a player can change what another player's report says. Ellis's "hugged" story also made it unclear whether a Floofer visit blocks an Eagle's gain.
Finley.fun: Round 3's day, where Ellis's Eagle, Kookaburra and Floofer stories collided and the table pieced together who was lying.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports more explicit about hugs and confusion, so players can check claimed visits against each other.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I threw at Drew on a weak read, and Drew was Farm. I would instead have kept my cards and waited for Drew's second visit to be checked.
